key_insight: MethylVI is a deep generative model that explicitly models the technical noise and biological variability in single-cell bisulfite sequencing (scBS-seq), producing denoised, imputed methylation probabilities and probabilistic latent embeddings for robust downstream analysis.
problem_solved: scBS-seq data are extremely sparse and noisy (variable coverage, conversion/efficiency artifacts, missing CpG calls), which hampers clustering, trajectory inference, and differential methylation analysis; existing methods do not jointly model count-level technical effects and cell-level biology.
method: Variational autoencoder framework that learns low-dimensional latent representations of cells from scBS-seq data.

Probabilistic observation model for bisulfite sequencing that accounts for per-site coverage, conversion/efficiency and overdispersion, enabling uncertainty-aware methylation probability estimates and imputation.
Batch- and covariate-aware training producing denoised methylation profiles, posterior uncertainties, and embeddings usable for clustering, trajectory inference, and differential testing.
impact: Provides ML practitioners with a principled, uncertainty-aware tool for sparse epigenomic data, improving downstream tasks (clustering, integration, differential analysis) and serving as a template for modeling technical noise in other single-cell modalities.
visual_elements: Model schematic: encoder → latent space → decoder with an overlay showing the bisulfite observation model (coverage + conversion parameters).
Before/after heatmaps of methylation calls (raw sparse counts vs. denoised/imputed methylation probabilities).
UMAP/TSNE of learned latent embeddings colored by cell type and batch to show separation and batch correction.
Bar/violin plots or calibration plots showing posterior uncertainty and improved differential methylation detection rates.
paper_title: Probabilistic modelling of single-cell bisulfite sequencing data with MethylVI
paper_authors: Ethan Weinberger, Wei Qiu, Wei Tian, Qiurui Zeng, Can Ergen
